prompt: Write a method that decides whether an int is a prime number. Complete the isPrime method in the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: Guard clauses handle the easy cases first: anything below 2 is rejected immediately with return false. The loop then tries each candidate divisor, and returning false the moment one divides n evenly short-circuits the rest of the work. Checking divisors only while i * i <= n is enough, because any factor larger than the square root would pair with one smaller than it. 91 = 7 * 13 is the classic trap that catches solutions that stop testing too early.
hints: Start with a guard clause: if (n < 2) return false;
Loop a candidate divisor i from 2 upward and return false as soon as n % i == 0.
You only need to test divisors while i * i <= n; if the loop finishes, return true.
